newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti sells OSR stake to Mannesmann.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti sells OSR stake to Mannesmann.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti said it had sold an 8.26 percent stake in Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari (OSR) to German engineering and telecoms company Mannesmann AG for 432.5 billion lire.
Olivetti said in a statement the sale did not change its position as the majority shareholder of OSR with a stake of 50.74 percent.
The sale value will enable Olivetti to report a capital gain of approximately 300 billion lire in its 1996 consolidated statements.
OSR owns 70 percent of Omnitel Pronto Italia (OPI), Italy's second GSM cellular telephone service operator. The other shareholder is consortium Pronto Italia which holds 30 percent.
Mannesmann Eurokom already holds a 19.82 percent stake in Pronto Italia, and through that stake had a shareholding in Omnitel Pronto Italia, before Friday's deal with Olivetti, of 5.9 percent.

Olivetti said the sale was subject to the pre-emptive rights of the other OSR shareholders, Bell Atlantic, Telia and CCIL, who had 30 days to exercise their rights on the same terms as those stipulated in the contract between Olivetti and Mannesmann.
It did not detail those terms but said, "This transaction means Mannesmann will now also enter OSR and appoint a representative on its board of directors."

Olivetti said 93 percent of the price, that is 404 billion lire, would be cashed in by the end of 1996. The remaining seven percent would be paid half in 1997 and the other half in 2001 at the latest, depending upon specific conditions of the purchase contract.

Olivetti also said that, separately, Pronto Italia's two main shareholders, AirTouch which holds 51.51 percent, and Mannesmann with 19.82 percent, increased their stake by purchasing shares or options from other owners.
It did not say what the new size of their stakes would be as a result of the transaction.

"In connection with these transactions, Olivetti has sold some option rights it owned in Pronto Italia for 50 billion lire," Olivetti said, adding this sum would be paid in full in 1996 and accounted for as income.

Joachim Funk, chief executive officer of Mannesmann, said the agreement "significantly strengthened its partnership and will enable us to increase our contribution to the future growth of Omnitel. We consider Omnitel a great success story."
Olivetti CEO Roberto Colannino said: "The operation greatly enhances the value of Olivetti's investment in Omnitel.
